Well, doctor, I... I guess I came in because things have just been so unsettling lately, and I just don't know what to do about it anymore. I work as a personal care aide, you know, helping folks out, and it's a very hard job. It takes a lot out of you, being on your feet and caring for people all day. So when I go home to my little studio apartment, I really just need some peace and quiet to recharge. 

But lately... well, I keep hearing these voices. And I don't mean like a radio left on next door or people talking out on the street. I mean it is as clear as somebody standing right there in my little studio with me. They keep saying my name, just over and over, and they keep telling me my work is being judged. Which just gets me so worked up and upset because I do right by my clients, I work so hard for them, but these voices are just right there judging everything I do. 

And the thing that really gets me is, I'll look around, I'll check the door, and the house is completely quiet. There is absolutely nobody there. Just me. But I hear them so plain, like they're right over my shoulder in the empty room, and it's just... it's driving me to my wit's end, having to deal with that when I'm just trying to get a moment of rest in my own home. I just can't take the judging when nobody is even in the room with me.

Well, I don't know anything about special powers or anything like that. I'm just a regular woman trying to pay her rent, doctor. But... well, there was this whole situation, and I still say I was right about it, even if nobody else wanted to hear it or believe me.

Anyway, a while back, I got it in my head—well, not just in my head, I knew it for an absolute fact—that the other home-care agency across town, the ones who drive those little green vans, and some people from the public library down the street, that they were watching my paintings and my client papers. 

I know how that sounds. I do. My sister, and even my neighbor Mrs. Higgins, they looked at me like I had grown a second head when I tried to warn them about it. They kept saying, 'Why on earth would the library ladies care about your little watercolors or your care logs? It makes no sense.' They told me I was just overtired from working too many double shifts. But they just didn't understand what was really going on, because they weren't the ones being targeted. 

Those people from the other agency and the library, they were watching my things to steal a chance that was meant for me. A really big opportunity. I don't know exactly how they were doing the watching, maybe through the windows or something else, but I could feel it, just like I know I'm sitting in this chair right now. They wanted to take this chance away from me, and they were using the library people to help them snoop on my private things. And even when folks told me it made absolutely no sense and told me to just put my papers in a drawer and forget about it, I still knew they were doing it. I mean, you can't just talk someone out of the truth, can you? I'd be sitting there, just trying to paint a nice picture of a daffodil to take my mind off my aching feet and the stress of the day, and I'd just know they were out there, plotting to steal my chance right out from under me. It's just exhausting, doctor, having to guard your own paperwork in your own home.

Oh, absolutely. One hundred percent. It is not just some passing thought, doctor, it is the absolute truth. 

Like I was saying just a minute ago, I got it in my head—well, people say 'got it in your head' like it's some silly daydream, but I didn't just imagine it, I *knew* it. I knew for a fact that the other home-care agency and those people from the library down the street were watching my paintings and my client papers. And they weren't just being nosey, either. They were watching my things to steal a chance that was meant for me. A really big chance. 

And it's exactly like you said, about people not believing it. Because even when folks told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. My sister would sit right there in my kitchen and say I was talking nonsense and tell me to just put my watercolors away, but you can't just tell someone the sky is green when they know it's blue, can you? I mean, when you work as an aide, you don't get a lot of big opportunities handed to you in this life. You're on your feet all day, lifting people heavier than you, cleaning up messes, and you're just exhausted down to your bones. So when a chance finally comes your way, of course you're going to notice when somebody is trying to snatch it right out from under you. 

So yes, I know it to be true. I don't care if Mrs. Higgins or my sister or the whole world tells me there's no reason to believe it, because I lived it. I knew they were watching me to steal my chance, and nothing anybody says is going to change the facts of what was going on right there in my own apartment.

Well, doctor, isn't that exactly what I've been trying to tell you this whole time? So yes, that's exactly what I've experienced. People just don't understand, and I can't exactly prove it to them in a court of law, but that doesn't make it any less true.

Well, calm is... I mean, I don't know if I'd ever call my life completely calm, doctor, because like I said, working as an aide is just a heavy, heavy load. I thought to myself, okay, finally, a little peace and quiet. I can just do my shifts, come home, do my watercolors, get my sleep. Just a normal, stable routine, right? 

But it didn't make a lick of difference. Even with me sleeping fine and having my energy back down to a normal level, the whole thing kept going. For several weeks, actually! Several weeks of just... well, it was exhausting. The voices were still right there in my quiet apartment, judging everything I did, picking apart my work and my care logs just like before. And that whole situation—my belief that those people were judging or tracking my work? That didn't stop either. 

You'd think if it was just stress or being tired, it would go away when you get some good sleep, right? That's what my sister kept telling me. She'd sit there and say, 'Just get some sleep, you're just overworked, it'll all blow over.' But I was sleeping! I was sleeping perfectly fine, my energy was completely normal, and for weeks and weeks, I still had to deal with the voices and the tracking. So it's not just stress, doctor. It doesn't matter if my life is stable or if I'm getting my rest, they just won't leave me be. It just proves that it's really happening, don't you think? Because if it was just in my head from being tired, a good eight hours of sleep would have fixed it, but it didn't change a thing.

Well, doctor, I really feel like I'm repeating myself here, because I swear I just went over this with you, but yes. Absolutely yes. I know what I know. Like I was saying before, I got it in my head—and I say that, but I mean I know it for an absolute fact—that the other home-care agency, you know, the ones driving those big green vans that they always park terribly, and some of those people from the library were watching my paintings and my client papers. I still know it. You can't just erase the truth just because other people are too blind to see it. So yes, I believe it completely, because it is completely true, no matter how many times I have to sit here and explain it.

Oh, doctor, let me tell you about that, because it’s a whole rollercoaster, it really is. You ask about feeling high or excited or not sleeping... well, yes, I definitely get exactly like that. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Doctor, I... I honestly don't know how many different ways I can explain this to you today. I feel like a broken record, I really do. You keep asking me about being shown I was wrong and if it changed my mind about other things, but you're missing the whole point. You're assuming I ever believed their so-called proof in the first place! 

Like I've been telling you all morning, I got it firmly in my head that the other home-care agency—the ones with those loud green vans—and those specific people from the library were watching my paintings and snooping on my client papers. And I know exactly why they were doing it. They were trying to steal a chance that was meant for me. My one big opportunity! After all the years I've spent working as an aide, breaking my back lifting people, making sure they don't slip in the shower, keeping track of every little thing on those logs... I earned that chance. 

So when folks sat me down, like Brenda did, and tried to tell me it made absolutely no sense for library workers to care about my watercolors or my daily logs... well, it didn't change my mind about that, and it certainly didn't make me question anything else I knew to be true. Why would it? If someone tries to tell you the sky is green, you don't suddenly start doubting that the grass is green too, do you? You just know they're talking nonsense. Even when folks told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. I knew it right down to my toes. Well, yes, actually. Yes, I have. It’s... it’s like a switch flips inside me, doctor. And it’s not because I won the lottery or because someone spilled coffee on my favorite scrub top, it just happens all on its own. 

Sometimes, I wake up and I just feel so... bright. That’s the only word for it. And I was so irritable the rest of the day, just pacing around her living room, wanting to crawl out of my own skin. 

So, yes, it goes from that huge, bright, chosen feeling where I’m going to conquer Greenville, right down to biting someone's head off over a simple question, and there's never a good reason for any of it starting in the first place. It just takes over.

That breakroom always smells like burnt popcorn because nobody watches the microwave, but anyway, Brenda sat me down and she talked to me for nearly an hour. She brought up every reason under the sun why she thought I was wrong. She told me it made absolutely no sense for anyone at a library to care about my watercolor paintings or my daily client logs. She went on and on about how everyone is just too busy with their own lives to be tracking mine.\n\nBut even when folks like Brenda and my sister told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. I didn't doubt it for a single moment, doctor. Not one. I know when someone is trying to take what is mine, and no amount of maps or schedules is going to make me ignore the truth of what I am living through every single day.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of a time when your belief about being watched or having your work judged occurred completely on its own, without being tied to how you were feeling emotionally or how much stress you were under at the time?\n\nPatient: Well, you know, people always want to blame stress. They think, oh, she's just working too many double shifts, she's lifting Mr. Henderson who weighs a good two hundred pounds and she's just exhausted. Or they think it's because I get in one of those bright, electric moods I was just telling you about, where I'm pacing the kitchen all night and not sleeping a wink. But no, doctor, that's not it at all. It's not just my mood playing tricks on me, and I can prove it to you. \n\nBecause I remember, very clearly, there was this one stretch... let's see, it was right after one of those really high-energy times. My energy had finally dropped back down, you know? The electricity was gone. I wasn't buzzing around the apartment anymore. I was actually sleeping normally again, getting a solid seven or eight hours, waking up, going to work, coming home, making my chamomile tea... just a regular, quiet routine. I wasn't feeling high or agitated or irritable at all. I felt completely level. \n\nBut those people from the library and the other agency? They didn't stop. And the voices—because, yes, I hear them talking about it, whispering and commenting on my client logs and my watercolors—the voices and that absolute certainty that they were judging and tracking my work, well, that just kept right on going. It didn't stop just because I finally got some sleep. It kept going for several weeks, completely on its own, even when I was perfectly calm. I would wake up, fully rested, feeling totally fine emotionally, not a drop of stress in my body, and I'd still hear them. I'd still know they were sneaking around, trying to steal my opportunity. So it has absolutely nothing to do with how stressed I am or if my mood is up or down. It just stays right there with me, day after day, for weeks at a time, because it's the truth of what's happening.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any time when your belief about being watched or having your work judged was challenged directly by something you experienced yourself, not just what others said, and if so, did it change your belief at all?\n\nPatient: Well, doctor, I know we keep circling back around to this, and I feel like I'm just talking your ear off about the exact same thing, but it’s just... it's my life, you know? It's what I'm dealing with every single day. You're asking if I ever saw something with my own two eyes that should have made me think differently. And, well, yes, I suppose I did try to play detective myself once. \n\nBecause, like I was just saying a few minutes ago, I got it so deep in my head that the other home-care agency and those specific people from the library were watching my paintings and snooping around my client papers. I knew they were doing it to steal a chance that was meant for me, and me alone. I just knew it. So, one morning before I went over to help Mrs. Gable—she’s another one of my clients, sweet lady, but she needs a whole lot of help getting her compression socks on, it takes me a good twenty minutes just to get them over her heels—I decided to set a little trap. I took a single strand of hair from my hairbrush, just one little gray hair, and I laid it ever so carefully right across my client logs and my watercolor pad on the kitchen table. I figured, if they are coming in here to look at my things, they'll brush that hair right off and I'll know for sure. \n\nWell, I came home after a long, long day. My feet were just aching, I was bone tired. I walked in, didn't even take my coat off, and went straight over to that table. And doctor, the hair was exactly where I left it. Not moved a fraction of an inch. Everything was completely untouched. \n\nSo there it was, right? My own little test showing nothing. And you know, even when folks told me it made no sense before, and now here I was looking at my own test that made it seem like nobody had been there... I still knew they were doing it. It didn't change my mind one single bit. I just stood there looking at that piece of hair and thought, well, they must be using tiny cameras, or they have some way of looking through the windows when I'm not paying attention, or they're just getting more clever about it. Because you can't tell me it isn't happening. I don't care if the hair didn't move, and I don't care if it seems to make no sense to anyone else. I know they are watching my work to take my opportunity, and absolutely nothing I see or don't see is going to wipe that truth away.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any experience, even a small one, that made you doubt your belief, even for a moment, that you were being watched or that your work was being judged?\n\nPatient: Doctor, I feel like we are just going round and round in circles today, I really do. You keep asking if I ever doubted it, if there was even one tiny little second where I thought, well, maybe I am just imagining things. And I have to tell you, the answer is just plain no. \n\nBecause, like I have been trying to explain to you this whole time, I got it in my head that the other home-care agency—the ones who drive those awful bright green vans around town—and some of those people from the library were watching my paintings and my client papers. And they aren't just doing it for fun, they are doing it to steal a chance that was meant for me. That is my chance, my opportunity, after all my years of hard work as an aide, wiping down counters and lifting heavy patients and making sure everyone else is taken care of. \n\nI have had plenty of people try to talk me out of it, so it's not like I haven't heard the other side. It's not just my sister or Mrs. Higgins trying to play detective. My supervisor at work, Brenda, she sat me down in the breakroom just last week. That breakroom always smells like burnt popcorn because nobody watches the microwave, but anyway, Brenda sat me down and she talked to me for nearly an hour. She brought up every reason under the sun why she thought I was wrong. She told me it made absolutely no sense for anyone at a library to care about my watercolor paintings or my daily client logs. She went on and on about how everyone is just too busy with their own lives to be tracking mine.\n\nBut even when folks like Brenda and my sister told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. I didn't doubt it for a single moment, doctor. Not one. Because when you know the truth, when you live with it every day and you see how they are trying to take what is rightfully yours, someone telling you it doesn't make sense just sounds like foolishness. You could bring the whole town in here to tell me I'm wrong, and I would still know exactly what they are up to. So no, no doubts at all. Not even a small one.\n\nDoctor: Have there ever been two full weeks in a row when you did not experience any of these voices or the feeling of being watched or targeted?\n\nPatient: Two full weeks? Oh, doctor, I wish. I really, truly wish I could sit here and tell you that I got a break like that, even just for a few days, let alone two whole weeks. But no, there hasn't been a break at all. Not a single one. Because... well, if I really sit back and count the time, these voices talking about me, and those fixed fears I have about my work being watched and judged—it has been happening for about nine months now. Nine whole months, doctor. \n\nI remember because it was right around the time I had to buy my new white non-slip shoes for my shifts. I was doing a lot of mornings with Mr. Henderson back then, and you know how hard it is on your feet, standing on that hard linoleum all day, making sure he doesn't slip in the bathroom. I remember bringing those shoes home, setting them by the front door, and that's when it really settled in. The whispering. The feeling of eyes just boring into the back of my neck while I was doing my client logs. And since that day, nine months ago, it hasn't stopped for a weekend, it hasn't stopped for a holiday, it hasn't stopped for a single week, let alone two. \n\nIt's just a constant, everyday thing now. You wake up, you make your chamomile tea, you hear them. You go to work, you wipe down the counters, you feel them watching your every move. Month after month after month. So when you ask if I've had two weeks without it, I just have to shake my head, because nine months is a long time to carry this around every single minute of the day. They are just relentless, they really are, and I keep trying to explain to people how exhausting it is to have your work scrutinized like that for almost a whole year, but nobody seems to... well, nobody seems to grasp just how long nine months really feels when you're going through it.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any time when you believed something so strongly that, even when you saw clear proof it wasn’t true, you still knew in your heart that it was?\n\nPatient: Well, doctor, I feel like we are just beating a dead horse here, because that's exactly what I've been trying to tell you this whole entire time. We keep coming back to this idea of proof, but what does 'clear proof' even mean when you just know something in your bones? \n\nI mean, I already told you about the little hair I left on the table, and how it didn't move. I just knew they were doing it, doctor, plain and simple, and no piece of evidence was ever going to make me believe otherwise.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a time when you were clearly shown that one of your beliefs was wrong, and if so, did that change how you thought about other similar beliefs you had?\n\nPatient: Doctor, I... You're assuming I ever believed their so-called proof in the first place! \n\nLike I've been telling you all morning, I got it firmly in my head that the other home-care agency—the ones with those loud green vans—and those specific people from the library were watching my paintings and snooping on my client papers. And I know exactly why they were doing it. They were trying to steal a chance that was meant for me. My one big opportunity! After all the years I've spent working as an aide, breaking my back lifting people, making sure they don't slip in the shower, keeping track of every little thing on those logs... Why would it? If someone tries to tell you the sky is green, you don't suddenly start doubting that the grass is green too, do you? You just know they're talking nonsense. Even when folks told me it made no sense, I still knew they were doing it. I knew it right down to my toes. So no, nobody showing me their version of the truth changed how I thought about any of it, because I was never wrong to begin with.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a time when your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable, even when nothing particularly exciting or upsetting was happening in your life?\n\nPatient: Well, yes, actually. I’ll start thinking about all the ways I’m going to reorganize my clients' schedules, and how I’m going to paint a mural on the side of the senior center, and how I need to write letters to the mayor about the sidewalks... it’s just this huge, rushing feeling of excitement and power, and nothing even caused it! \n\nBut then... and this is the hard part to explain to people who haven't felt it... it can turn so fast. And I was so irritable the rest of the day, just pacing around her living room, wanting to crawl out of my own skin. \n\nSo, yes, it goes from that huge, bright, chosen feeling where I’m going to conquer Greenville, right down to biting someone's head off over a simple question, and there's never a good reason for any of it starting in the first place. It just takes over.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a time when you believed something so strongly that even when you saw clear proof it wasn't true, you still knew in your heart that it was?\n\nPatient: Doctor, we just went over this, didn't we? My watercolors, the ones I do in the evenings when I finally get to sit down. And they were watching my client papers, too. My logs, my schedules, all of it. And they were doing it to steal a chance that was meant for me! I know it sounds crazy to you, and it sounded crazy to Brenda, and everybody else who tried to tell me it made absolutely no sense. They all tried to give me their \"proof,\" telling me that library workers don't care about home-care logs, and that the other agency doesn't even know who I am. \n\nBut like I keep saying, it didn't matter what they said. It didn't matter what \"clear proof\" they thought they had. I just knew they were doing it. I could feel it in my bones.
